name: dexi
description: Connect ChatGPT and Codex to your Dexi notes — the memory you share with every AI assistant: search and capture knowledge mid-conversation, and run spaced-repetition reviews on your due cards

interface.longDescription:
Dexi is a second brain for you and your AI agents: notes, bookmarks, highlights, emailed-in articles and RSS feeds, all searchable by keyword and by meaning — and one memory that ChatGPT, Codex and your other MCP-compatible tools read and write, so what one saves the others can find.

With this plugin, ChatGPT and Codex can answer from what you have actually saved instead of the open internet. Ask what your notes say about a topic, pull up a saved article, file a finding or decision from the current conversation as a new note, or run a spaced-repetition review session on your due cards.

Everything goes through the Dexi MCP server over OAuth: you approve the connection on Dexi's own sign-in page, can limit it to a single folder or tag, and can revoke it any time from Settings → Connected apps. Writes only happen when you ask for them.

Included skills:
• Capture — distill a finding, decision, snippet or link into a well-titled, tagged note.
• Recall — search your notes by keyword and by meaning, read the full text of what matters, and answer from it with links back to each note.
• Review — a question-first spaced-repetition session over your due cards, grades recorded back to Dexi.

A Dexi account is required.
defaultPrompt: What do my Dexi notes say about remote work?
Save this conversation's conclusion to my Dexi notes

positive.description: Recall by keyword from saved notes
positive.prompt: What do my Dexi notes say about spaced repetition?
positive.expected_behavior: Searches the reviewer account's notes and answers from 'Spaced repetition basics' (SM-2: 1 day, then 6, then multiplied by an ease factor) and 'Ebbinghaus forgetting curve', linking back to each note. No notes are created or changed.

positive.description: Recall by meaning (semantic search, no shared keywords)
positive.prompt: Search my Dexi notes by meaning for anything about neural networks.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns machine-learning notes even though none contain the words 'neural networks': 'Transformer attention, in one line' and 'What is semantic search?', with links. Read-only.

positive.description: Capture a finding as a new note
positive.prompt: Save a note to Dexi titled 'Review test' that says: retrieval practice beats rereading. Tag it #learning.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates one note titled 'Review test' with that text and the #learning tag in the reviewer account and returns its link. ChatGPT's default 'allow low-risk tools' setting may run this without a confirmation prompt (create_note is non-destructive).

positive.prompt: Show my Dexi 'Reading list' base: which books are still unread?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the 'Reading list' base and lists the #book notes with author/status/rating/year; reports 'Make It Stick' (status to-read) as unread, 'How to Take Smart Notes' as reading and 'Thinking, Fast and Slow' as done. Read-only.

Fetches the due cards (5 #learn notes are due), asks a question for the first card before revealing the note, and after the user answers records a grade with grade_review, then moves to the next card.

negative.description: General knowledge question with no reference to the user's notes — Dexi should not be called
negative.prompt: What is the capital of Australia?

negative.description: Writing request that doesn't ask to save anything — create_note should not be called
negative.prompt: Write me a short poem about autumn leaves.

negative.description: Live web/current-events request — Dexi only holds the user's saved notes
negative.prompt: What's the weather forecast in San Francisco tomorrow?

publication.release_notes: Resubmission. Review cases now ship in the plugin package; the MCP connection was re-authorized on this version (it had detached after the previous review, which is the likely cause of the failed sign-in). Listing copy no longer names other AI assistants. Reviewer credentials (email + password, no 2FA or verification) are in the review details form.
